## The path from "due date passes" to "assignee sees an alert once"

**What starts the check.** `src/instrumentation.ts`'s `register()` runs once when the Next.js server process boots (Node runtime only) and calls two things: `registerEventHandlers()` (`src/server/services/event-registry.ts`) and `startScheduler()` (`src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts`). `startScheduler()` sets a `setInterval` firing every 60 seconds that calls `tick(now)`. `tick()` checks `isDue("overdue-issues", now)` against `CADENCE_MINUTES["overdue-issues"] = 60`, and once an hour it calls `enqueue({ kind: "overdue-issues", ... })` before calling `drain()`. `src/server/jobs/queue.ts`'s `drain()` pulls the due job and dynamically imports/invokes `runOverdueIssueJob(now)` from `src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts` — that's the actual entry point of the sweep.

**Narrowing the set of issues that count.** `runOverdueIssueJob` loops over orgs (`usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup`, batched 50 at a time) and, per org, calls `issueRepo.listOverdueIssues(orgId, now)` in `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`. That query filters to: tenant-scoped, not archived (`livePredicate`), has a due date (`isNotNull(issues.dueAt)`), due date in the past (`lt(issues.dueAt, now)`), and status still open (`inArray(issues.status, ["backlog","todo","in_progress","in_review"])`) — closed/done/resolved issues are excluded. The job adds a redundant null-check on `dueAt` as a belt-and-suspenders guard.

**What the checking component does and doesn't own.** For each qualifying issue, `runOverdueIssueJob` does not send any notification or touch email/in-app delivery itself — it only calls `emit("issue.overdue", { orgId, actorId: null, issueId, projectId, dueAt, assigneeId, ... })` via `src/lib/event-bus.ts`. Formatting, channel selection, and delivery are explicitly left to whoever subscribes to that event; the job's job is just to detect and announce.

**Stopping repeat announcements.** Inside `overdue-issue-job.ts` there's a module-scoped `reported = new Set<string>()`. Before emitting for an issue, the job checks `if (reported.has(issue.id)) continue;`, and adds the id after a successful emit. This is in-memory/process-lifetime dedup (not a DB column), so a process restart could in theory re-announce an issue that's still overdue — but within a running process the same overdue issue is only emitted once. A separate, persisted dedup exists further downstream for the digest email path: `notifications.readAt` (`src/server/db/schema/notifications.ts`) gets set by the digest job so the same digest window doesn't email twice, but that's about the digest bundle, not the original overdue event.

**Reaching the one assignee through their chosen channels.** `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` registers a fan-out subscriber (`registerFanOut`, run once at module load) on `"issue.overdue"`: if `payload.assigneeId` is null it does nothing; otherwise it calls `notify(orgId, "issue_overdue", [assigneeId], {...})`. `notify()` looks up that user's row via `preferenceRepo.getPreference` (`src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts`), then `resolveChannels(preference, flags)` computes their channels: defaults to `["in_app", "email"]` if no preference exists; otherwise `in_app` is included if `preference.inApp`, and `email` is included only if `preference.email` and the user isn't `digestOnly` (unless the `digest_email` flag is on, in which case `digestOnly` users get it bundled instead). If no channels resolve, nothing is written for that user. The result is persisted via `notificationRepo.insertNotifications` (`src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts`) as a row with a `channels` JSON column on `notifications`. In-app delivery is just the client reading that row (`src/hooks/use-notifications.ts`, rendered in `notification-bell.tsx`/`notification-list.tsx` via `notificationService.listNotifications`). Email delivery, notably, only actually happens through the digest path — `src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts`'s `runDigestEmailJob` picks up digest subscribers, bundles unread notifications via `digest-service.ts`, and sends via `email-service.ts`'s `sendEmail()`; there's a dedicated `src/emails/overdue-email.tsx` template registered in `render.ts`/`email-service.ts`'s template unions, but nothing ever calls `sendEmail` with `template: "overdue"` — so an immediate per-issue overdue email is not currently wired, only the digest is.
